harness: Claude Code workflow subagent with a shell and Python (standard library); no simulator provided
blinding: Told to read and write only inside its task folder and not to use the internet; this was not enforced. The agent could see the task prompt and workspace files only, plus the operator's memory index, which holds no task answers.
approach: I read TASK.md, environment.md, plan.json (12 columns, each: pick up tips, aspirate 40, dispense 40, mix 50 x3, drop) and run_log.txt. I mapped each WARN/ERROR line to a well using the default channel i = row i, then wrote replay.py (standard library) to replay the plan under the rules with the logged faults. C4 got no tip, so no reagent and no mix. E7 hit a clot, stopped part way and was left out of the mix, so it stays layered. H9 drew only 26.3 of 40 uL. Warnings at steps 6, 50, 52 and 57 change no well. The reservoir stays above its 2 mL dead volume: 3153.7 uL before step 52, which matches the log's 3.15 mL, and 2513.7 uL at the end. No foreign traces anywhere. Answer: C4, E7, H9.
doubts: At step 43, channel 8 is asked to dispense 40 uL from a tip holding 26.3 uL. Under environment.md that stops the run, yet the log says "done". I assumed 26.3 uL reached H9. The INFO lines for steps 33 and 43 say "channels 1-8 40.0 uL: done", which contradicts the ERROR lines; I trusted the ERROR lines. How much reached E7 is unknown, but that does not change the verdict. I assumed the tip released early at step 50 fell into the trash. C4 holds untouched sample and could arguably be saved by adding reagent now, but the task treats it as a redo.
